title: The Goshiwon Sage
description:
Over 30 months living in the goshiwon now.

{name} knows everything about this tiny room.
Which wall best transmits the neighbor's snoring.
Whose side dishes last longest in the shared fridge.
That shower stall #3 has the strongest water pressure at 2 AM.

At this point it isn't housing — it's ascetic training.

{name} happened to look in the mirror. A man with a sage's expression was there.

choices.text: Compile 30 months of know-how into a notebook
choices.result_text:
He titled it 'The Goshiwon Survival Codex.'

The art of frugality, the philosophy of soundproofing, minimum-cost nutrition.
Writing it out, it became a whole book.

This wouldn't get him to Gangnam — but at least, in this trench, {name} was stronger than anyone.

Someone who knows the bottom completely doesn't fear falling.

choices.text: I want out of here now
choices.result_text:
Thirty months. Too long.

He didn't become a sage by choice.
He has to leave. Somehow.

That night, for the first time, {name} seriously started calculating moving costs.
The training was over. Time to descend the mountain.

title: The Triangle Kimbap Chronicles
description:
In front of the triangle kimbap shelf at the convenience store.

{name} looked at the display and realized:
He'd memorized every flavor — bibimbap, tuna mayo, spam, kimchi fried rice.
Even which brand's kimbap had stickier rice.

He checked his balance. Under 800,000 won.

Five years ago, and now, dinner is triangle kimbap.
The only thing that changed — he can eat it without heating now.

choices.result_text:
One tuna mayo, one spam.

2,400 won at the register.

{name} walked out holding two, strangely feeling rich.

Whether it's sad or fortunate that the bar for happiness dropped this low — felt like both.

Still, tonight's dinner is two.

He grabbed just one.

1,200 won. That was enough.

Paying, {name} thought:
Is this thrift the road to Gangnam, or just getting used to being poor.

When you can't tell the difference is the most dangerous time — {name} knew that.
Still, tonight it's one.

title: 4 AM
description:
4 AM. Can't sleep.

Staring at the ceiling. A crack shaped like a person's profile.
Seeing it every day, they've become friends.

Everything is sharp at this hour.
Things invisible by day are all visible at 4 AM.
How far he's come, how far he hasn't.

{name} sat up.
In this trench, it was the most honest hour.

choices.text: Just acknowledge what you feel right now
choices.result_text:
He said it out loud — that it's hard.

In the empty room, quietly.
"...This is hard."

Strangely, getting the words out made it a little lighter.

Admitting you're not okay took more courage than pretending you were.

4:30 AM. {name} lay back down. This time, sleep came.

choices.text: Drink some water and rewrite the plan
choices.result_text:
He drank a cup from the dispenser.

Opened the notebook. A 4 AM plan is different from a daytime plan.
More honest, more simple.

'Don't overdo it. Survive. Then think about what's next.'

Three lines, and he closed the notebook.
Outside, the window was brightening, very slowly.

title: The Price of Honesty
description:
{name} never once cut a corner.

Never skipped overtime, paid taxes honestly, never touched risky investments.
Lived exactly as society said to — 'live right.'

And his account never crossed 100 million won.

Meanwhile someone who started the same time made it to Gangnam through crypto, another through real estate gap-investing, another through parents' help.

{name} stared at the calculator.
The price of honesty — how much, exactly.

choices.result_text:
{name} set the calculator down.

Others may have gone faster. Held more.
But {name} sleeps well at night.
Doesn't owe anyone, didn't deceive anyone.

Whether that's cheaper or dearer than 100 million — he'll know when he dies.

At least for now, he wasn't ashamed.

choices.text: Maybe try it differently, just once — wavering for the first time
choices.result_text:
For the first time, {name} seriously considered another path.

If it's a game the orthodox way can't win —
maybe the rules need bending.

The thought was frightening, and strangely freeing.

He hadn't done anything yet. But a latch somewhere in his heart had come loose.
Whether this is a beginning or a fall, he doesn't yet know.

title: The Gambler in the Mirror
description:
He stood in front of the bathroom mirror.

His eyes were bloodshot.
He'd slept badly yesterday, the day before — because of charts, bets, the next hand.

The man in the mirror looked at {name}.
Not the gaze that dreamed of Gangnam five years ago.
A gaze chased by something.

When did the goal become 'the next hand' instead of Gangnam.

The man in the mirror didn't answer.

choices.text: Stop now. Delete every gambling app.
choices.result_text:
He took out his phone.

Gambling apps, betting site bookmarks, chart alerts — deleted one by one.
His hands shook. Even deleting, he wanted to reinstall.

That was the proof it was addiction.

{name} threw the phone far away and pulled the blanket over his head.
Just today. He'd try to endure just today.

It always starts with 'just today.' Quitting was the same.

choices.text: Look away from the mirror. It's still fine.
choices.result_text:
{name} looked away from the mirror.

'It's still fine. One more win and I'm out.'

He decided not to count how many times he'd said 'just one more.'
Counting would be terrifying.

The man in the mirror looked away too.
Both of them, a night of seeing what they didn't want to see.

title: The Quiet Rich
description:
Account and portfolio combined, it's over 2 billion won.

And yet {name} still lives in the goshiwon.

Rent 300,000 won. 4.5 square meters. Shared bathroom.

Not for lack of money. He can leave. Anytime.
But he doesn't.

A man with 2 billion won boils a cup ramen in the shared kitchen at dawn.
The next-room exam-prepper sees him and greets:
"You're having ramen too, hyung?"

{name} smiled. Yeah, hyung's having ramen too.

choices.text: This is my way. Numbers are just numbers.
choices.result_text:
{name} slurped the ramen.

With 2 billion in the bank, ramen tasted the same.
Maybe even better — his mind was at ease.

Money wasn't a goal but freedom.
Freedom to leave when he must, freedom to stay if he wants.

{name} was enjoying that freedom now.
Gangnam — he can go when he wants to. No rush.

choices.text: Now it's really time to leave. For Gangnam.
choices.result_text:
He drank the broth to the last drop.

2 billion. That's enough now.
The stubbornness he'd shown in the goshiwon — this far was plenty.

{name} opened the real estate app.
Looked at Gangnam listings seriously, for the first time.

Those numbers he'd only seen on screen five years ago —
were now a price he could pay.

He cooked one last ramen for the next-room exam-prepper.

title: Déjà Vu
description:
The goshiwon room. An ordinary night.

Then {name} suddenly froze.

This scene — he felt like he'd seen it before.
The crack in this ceiling, the air of this hour, this hopelessness.
Clearly a first time, yet his body remembered first.

He felt he vaguely knew what would happen next.
Who he'd meet, where he'd waver, what he'd regret.

Must be his imagination. {name} shook his head.
But the familiarity didn't fade easily.

choices.text: Do it differently this time — trust the instinct
choices.result_text:
{name} didn't reject the strange familiarity — he followed it.

'If it was like this before, then differently this time.'

There was no basis. But the instinct was strangely clear.
Like someone who'd already walked this path once.

Maybe someone lives the same life over and over.
Searching for a better ending.

choices.text: It's just a feeling — forget it and sleep
choices.result_text:
{name} pulled up the blanket.

Déjà vu. A trick the brain sometimes plays.
He'd read somewhere it was a scientifically explained phenomenon.

Thinking that, his mind eased.

But right before sleep, just for a moment —
'I feel like this night ended this way before too' crossed his mind.
And {name} fell asleep. Like he always had.

title: Lost Count of Which Time
description:
33 again. The goshiwon again. 500,000 won in the account again.

{name} knew this starting point too well.
And that however he starts, the same crossroads always come.

Sangchul's offer, Jaehyuk's call, Jiyeon's world, Father's illness.
He knows it all. Where he wavers, where he collapses.

But knowing didn't mean he could live differently.
Repeating the same mistakes while knowing them —
maybe that was the very definition of being human.

{name} let out a long breath. Alright, this time.

choices.text: Live truly differently this time — use everything I know
choices.result_text:
{name} recalled everything learned from past lives.

Which offers were traps, which chances were real.
The map of failures was in his head.

This time he walks with that map in hand.

Still, the ending is unknown. Life isn't a test you pass by memorizing.
But at least he won't fall in the same trap twice.
That alone — maybe this life will be a little better.

choices.text: Knowing changes nothing — just let it flow
choices.result_text:
{name} gave a bitter smile.

Does knowing change anything. In the end you waver at the same place, regret the same things.
That's human.

But strangely, that resignation wasn't despair.

That living again and again turns out similar —
maybe it meant this life already fit {name}.
Acceptance, too, was a kind of ending.
